candidates.title: Why Everyone Keeps Buying the F-35 Despite Its Problems
candidates.central_question: How can GAO call the F-35 DOD's most expensive weapon system and flag years of readiness problems, while allies still line up to buy it?
candidates.angle: Explain the sensor-fusion and networking logic that buyers are actually paying for. Contrast it with sustainment costs and the TR-3/Block 4 delays, and show that the purchase is a membership in an alliance data network, not just a jet.
key_sources: GAO-23-105341, F-35 Aircraft: DOD and the Military Services Need to Reassess the Future Sustainment Strategy
DOT&E Annual Report, F-35 section (annual)
F-35 Joint Program Office Selected Acquisition Report
risks: Program cost figures must be lifecycle vs acquisition labeled clearly
Avoid partisan framing of foreign sales
Classified capabilities stated only as attributed estimates

candidates.title: Why the Navy Still Builds Carriers China Can Target from Shore
candidates.central_question: China has fielded missiles designed to hit carriers from over a thousand miles away, so why is the US still building $13 billion Ford-class ships?
candidates.angle: Walk the kill chain conceptually: find, fix, track, target, strike. Show that a missile's range only matters if every link holds. Then cover the honest limitation, which is that carriers may have to operate farther out, shrinking what their air wings can reach.
footage_evidence: archive probe "USS Gerald R. Ford flight operations": 50 results
key_sources: DoD Annual Report to Congress: Military and Security Developments Involving the People's Republic of China
CRS: Navy Ford (CVN-78) Class Aircraft Carrier Program: Background and Issues for Congress
Department of the Navy Shipbuilding and Conversion budget books
risks: DF-21D/DF-26 performance is unproven; frame as estimates attributed to DoD
Explain the kill chain conceptually only, with no exploitable specifics

candidates.title: Why Hypersonic Missiles Aren't as Unstoppable as Promised
candidates.central_question: If hypersonic missiles are fast enough to beat defenses, why was a Kinzhal intercepted over Kyiv, and why is the US still racing to build its own?
candidates.angle: Separate speed from maneuverability: ballistic missiles were already hypersonic. Explain the real advantages (low flight profile, maneuvering, tracking gaps) and the real costs (heat, guidance, price), then close on why the actual threat is detection time, not the label.
key_sources: CRS: Hypersonic Weapons: Background and Issues for Congress
CRS: Conventional Prompt Global Strike and Long-Range Ballistic Missiles
GAO reports on DoD hypersonic weapons programs
risks: Russian and Ukrainian intercept claims must be attributed as claims
Avoid 'unstoppable' framing except as a quoted claim being tested
Speeds and ranges of foreign systems are estimates

candidates.title: Why the Navy Fires Million-Dollar Missiles at Cheap Drones
candidates.central_question: Why does the US Navy keep using interceptors that cost far more than the drones they destroy, and what would it take to flip that math?
candidates.angle: Use the Red Sea campaign to explain cost-exchange ratios. Cover the layered defense chain (SM-2, ESSM, guns, aircraft, lasers), explain why cheaper options are not yet ready, and show why magazine depth, not hit rate, is the real limit.
key_sources: Department of the Navy Budget Estimates, Weapons Procurement, Navy (annual justification books)
CRS: Navy Shipboard Lasers: Background and Issues for Congress
U.S. Central Command press releases on Red Sea engagements
CRS: Houthi attacks on commercial shipping (In Focus series)
risks: Drone unit costs are estimates and must be presented as such
Houthi claims of hits must be attributed as claims
Do not list specific gaps in shipboard defense

candidates.title: Why Golden Dome Is Harder Than Hitting a Bullet with a Bullet
candidates.central_question: Missile interceptors can hit warheads in tests, so why is defending an entire country still considered one of the hardest problems in defense?
candidates.angle: Explain the intercept chain (detect, track, discriminate, intercept) and why each step gets harder against decoys, salvos and maneuvering warheads. Use the 2025 executive order as the hook, and close on cost and physics limits like space-based interceptor coverage.
footage_evidence: archive probe "Ground-based Midcourse Defense flight test": 11 results
key_sources: Executive Order 'The Iron Dome for America' (January 27, 2025)
GAO annual reports on Missile Defense Agency progress
Missile Defense Agency budget justification documents
risks: Golden Dome cost estimates are forecasts and must be attributed
Politically charged; keep to physics and budgets
No discussion of specific defensive gaps

candidates.title: Why Armies Are Still Buying Tanks in the Age of Drones
candidates.central_question: If cheap drones destroy tanks in Ukraine, why are the US Army and European armies spending billions on new ones?
candidates.angle: Explain what a tank does that nothing else does: protected mobile firepower for breakthroughs. Then show the Army's own response, which was to cancel SEPv4 for the lighter M1E3 redesign, and examine whether weight, sensors and active protection can restore the balance.
footage_evidence: archive probe "M1A2 Abrams live fire": 50 results
key_sources: U.S. Army press release on ending M1A2 SEPv4 and launching the M1E3 Abrams (September 2023)
CRS: The Army's M1 Abrams Tank (Issues for Congress)
RUSI reports on Russian and Ukrainian armour losses
risks: Ukraine combat footage has licensing and graphic-content issues; use only to explain
Loss counts are disputed; use the best-sourced figure with 'around'
No how-to on defeating specific armour

candidates.title: Why the Pentagon Can't Build Enough Artillery Shells
candidates.central_question: How did the world's largest defense budget end up unable to supply enough of a simple steel shell, and why does fixing it take years?
candidates.angle: Trace a 155mm shell through the industrial chain: forged steel bodies, explosive fill, a few government-owned plants and single-source chemicals. Explain why surge capacity was cut in peacetime and why money alone cannot make it reappear quickly.
footage_evidence: archive probe "155mm production Scranton Army Ammunition Plant": 1 results
key_sources: U.S. Army statements on 155mm production targets (Army Joint Program Executive Office Armaments & Ammunition)
CRS: U.S. Defense Industrial Base and munitions production reports
Army Procurement of Ammunition budget justification books
risks: Production targets are plans; attribute them as Army goals
Ukraine consumption rates vary; use the best-sourced figure

candidates.title: Why the Ocean Is Getting Harder to Hide In
candidates.central_question: Submarines have relied on the ocean's opacity for 70 years, so why is the US betting $130+ billion on new missile submarines just as sensors improve?
candidates.angle: Explain the acoustic mechanism: sound channels, quieting and passive sonar. Then show what is changing (satellites, unmanned sensors, data processing) and why the Columbia class and AUKUS are bets that stealth will outlast detection.
key_sources: CRS: Navy Columbia (SSBN-826) Class Ballistic Missile Submarine Program
CRS: Navy Virginia-Class Submarine Program and AUKUS Submarine Proposal
Department of the Navy shipbuilding budget books
risks: Submarine performance data is classified; frame as estimates only
Explain detection principles, not methods against named boats
